correctness.rationale: The Cesàro average is the sum of Schur squares of distinct-eigenvalue projectors; its quadratic form equals the sum of squared norms of E diag(x) E. For g≠1 the cross block has rank two and distinct positive singular values (the determinant is sqrt((a−1)(b−1))(g−1) and the off-diagonal entry of its left square is positive). The zero-energy constraints on each unmarked part give one singleton or contrast variable if its size is one or two, and no variable otherwise. The ±-paired nonzero-eigenvalue constraints can be checked independently using the diagonals of the support projector Q and H². For a,b≥3 these have marked-coordinate rows (1,1) and (g²+b−1,g²+a−1); the unmarked variables have zero mean. With either part of size 2, the marked and unmarked columns within that part give determinant ±(g²−1). These moment constraints yield exactly the asserted balanced exception and small-part contributions, including the deleted edge g=0. At g=1 the entire-part zero-sum subspace is dark; only a two-vertex contrast can survive in either part, and its part sum is zero so the bright constraints vanish. The rank drop and positive-definiteness statements follow. These analytic checks cover the quantifiers independently of the finite rational/spectral checks described by the frozen verifier, which was inspected rather than executed.

value.rationale: The average-mixing rank is a natural measure of linear distinguishability of the long-time position distributions. The classification identifies exactly which equal-size and small-part constraints survive a single coupling change, including why the rank can jump at the unit bond but does not vary with the strength of a nonunit bond. It treats the entire weighted family and gives a full-rank boundary, not just a few example matrices.
